Entries.Text: Bring materials from another project, a material file or a JSON export into this project. Each material is compared with the game's own, so only what the source changed is taken, and your own edits are kept. Review the plan, then Apply it as one undo step. Nothing is saved until you save.
Opens Material Merge in the Tools window.
Where the materials to merge come from.
A project of the same game. Only the material binders in its own folder are read: every other binder is the game's, so it has nothing to merge.
A loose .mtd or .matbin, matched to your material of the same name; or a whole binder (.mtdbnd, .matbinbnd), each material matched in your binder of the same file name. Compressed or not.
A material exported as JSON (Export or Copy as JSON), matched to your material of the name it records; or a set from Export Modified as JSON, each material put back in the binder it came from.
No other project of this game. Add one in the Project Editor.
Choose an .mtd or .matbin file, or a material binder.
The file isn't an MTD, a MATBIN or a binder of them.
The file isn't a material JSON export or set.
The export's param {0} has a type or value that doesn't fit.
Defaults for the plan. You can change each material's choice afterwards.
When both changed the same thing:
The default for conflicts: a param, sampler or texture you and the source both changed differently.
Keep your value in each conflict; their other changes are still merged.
Take their value in each conflict.
Leave materials with a conflict as they are, to decide one by one.
Add the materials only the source has. Off, they're listed but skipped.
Delete game materials the other project deleted from its binders. Materials you changed are never deleted by default.
Analyse builds the plan without changing anything. Apply makes it one undo step.
Compare the source with your materials and the game's, and list what merging would do.
Merge everything in the plan that isn't skipped or blocked, as one undo step. Materials you edited since the analysis are left alone.
What merging does to each material. Double-click a material to open it.
Choose a source and press Analyse.
{0} to add, {1} changed by them, {2} changed by both, {3} conflicts, {4} deleted by them. {5} need nothing.
The binder new materials go in when the source doesn't say which binder they belong to.
Keep your value in every conflict, and skip materials that can only be taken whole.
Take their value in every conflict, and their whole material where it can't be merged entry by entry.
In {0}. Double-click to open your material.
Only the source has this material.

You and the source changed the same param, sampler or texture differently. Choose per entry below.
You and the source both added a material by this name, differently. Choose per entry below.
You and the source both changed the shader. A material's params belong to its shader, so it can only be taken whole or skipped.
A param, sampler or texture name appears twice, so entries can't be matched. It can only be taken whole or skipped.
You deleted this game material, and the source changed it. Take theirs to add it back.
The other project deleted this material, but you changed it. It's kept unless you choose Delete.
Each header field, param, sampler or texture that differs, as the game, you and the source have it. Double-click an entry to find it in your material.
Your project already has {0} in another binder or folder ({1}). Models find materials by name, so two of one name can't both be used: merge into yours, add theirs under a numbered name, or skip.
The merged material has errors, so it won't be applied. Choose differently, or skip it.

Merged: {0} changed, {1} added, {2} deleted. {3} left alone (edited since the analysis), {4} not applied (errors, or no binder to add to).
